_readme: Per-county card copy for the Watchdog county-report carousel.
FIELDS
hook  - eyebrow / short line. 5-10 words. The thing that makes this county not another county.
note  - card body. 1-2 sentences. Replaces the old generic 'Explore ... with real evidence' text.
cta   - link label.
SOURCES
Municipality counts and general tax rates: tax-rates.json (NJ Division of Taxation,
General Tax Rates by County and Municipality, 2016-2025). Rates are per $100 of
assessed value. 'Median rate' is the median across that county's municipalities for 2025.
Equalization ratios: equalization-ratios.json (Chapter 123 certification, tax year 2026).
NOTE: that file currently covers only Atlantic, Burlington, Camden, Cape May, Cumberland,
Gloucester and Salem. Ratio claims appear only in those seven entries. Do not add ratio
language to the other fourteen until the file is extended.
TWO THINGS NOT TO SAY
1. A falling tax rate is not a tax cut. Monmouth (-24% median over five years) and
Somerset (-13%) reflect revaluations resetting assessed values, not lower bills.
Their copy is written around this on purpose.
2. A high nominal rate is not a high bill. Winfield (23.411), East Brunswick (12.177)
and Kearny (10.848) are real rates on very low assessed values. Never rank counties
by rate alone without the ratio.
REFRESH
Rates change annually, usually late summer. Ratios are certified each October 1 and can
be amended by the Tax Court into the following winter. Re-derive 'note' when either file
is updated. 'hook' is durable and rarely needs to change.

atlantic.note: Atlantic County has the most consistent upward rate pressure in South Jersey, with only one municipality avoiding an increase since 2020.

bergen.note: No county in New Jersey is more fragmented. Half its towns held rates flat over the last five years while the other half did not.

burlington.note: Burlington's median rate is up about 12% in five years, and it is one of the broadest counties in the state at 40 municipalities.

camden.note: Camden County taxes harder than any of its neighbors, among the steepest rates in New Jersey.

cape-may.note: Every one of Cape May's 16 municipalities raised rates since 2020, the only county in New Jersey where that is true.

cumberland.note: Cumberland's median ratio of 73% is the highest in South Jersey.

essex.note: Essex is unusual for North Jersey in how little movement there has been, with only 13 of 22 municipalities raising rates since 2020.

gloucester.note: Gloucester's assessments are pretty wild in this county.

hudson.note: Hudson is the smallest county by municipality count and one of the hardest to read from rates alone.

hunterdon.note: Hunterdon has been one of the steadier counties in the state, with ten of its 26 towns holding rates level since 2020.

mercer.note: All twelve Mercer municipalities increased their general tax rate since 2020, with a median rise of about 14%.

middlesex.note: Middlesex's 25 municipalities have a median rate of 4, up roughly 11% in five years.

monmouth.note: Monmouth's median rate dropped sharply over five years, but that is revaluation resetting assessed values across the county rather than anyone's bill going down.

morris.note: Morris with a moderate five-year climb, and its range is tighter than most large counties.

ocean.note: Ocean County is among the lowest in New Jersey, and it has also climbed about 16% in five years, one of the steeper increases in the state.

passaic.note: Passaic joins Cape May and Mercer as the only counties where every single municipality raised its rate since 2020.

salem.note: The county's median ratio of 70 is high by South Jersey standards, meaning assessments here already sit fairly close to market value.

somerset.note: Most Somerset municipalities show lower rates than they did in 2020, but that reflects revaluations raising assessed values rather than a genuine reduction.

sussex.note: Sussex's 24 municipalities have a median of 3.1, with about seven holding flat since 2020.

union.note: Union County's median general tax rate is the steepest of any New Jersey county a reminder that a rate means nothing without the ratio underneath it.

warren.note: Warren has among the most uniform upward pressure in North Jersey, with a median increase of about 14% since 2020 and only one municipality holding steady.
